newsitem.title: USA: Union accepts Sun Marcus Hook job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Union accepts Sun Marcus Hook job cuts.

text.p: Members of the Oil, Chemical and Atomic Workers Local 8-901 voted Tuesday to accept Sun Co Inc's proposal to cut 175 hourly positions at its Marcus Hook refinery.
The company had originally proposed trimming 235 positions at the facility, which has a refining capacity of 175,000 barrels per day.
The union's approval of the cutbacks put an end to fears the workers at the refinery would strike after Sun proposed stiff layoffs in early December.
Sun sought to cut costs at the refinery, which, along with its two-refinery Philadelphia facility, lost $44 million through the first nine months of 1996 and $37 million during all of 1995.
The job cuts at Marcus Hook will take place over the course of 1997 and will provide a severance package that allows 12 to 60 weeks pay depending on length of service.
